_doc: DECLARED divergences between .mergify.yml's `check-success=` conditions and the required checks
the `protect-dev` ruleset asks for in variables.tf. Read by scripts/ci/check-required-checks.mjs.
ONLY ONE DIRECTION CAN BE DECLARED, and the asymmetry is the point.
A check Mergify waits for that the ruleset does not yet require is SAFE — Mergify simply holds
the PR until it is green — and it is the repo's documented order: list it here first, apply the
ruleset after, so that a PR which genuinely fails the new gate is held visibly rather than
queued and then refused. `capabilities-security` and `Build console images (no push)` both went
in that way. That state is temporary by design, which is exactly why it has to be written down:
an undeclared lead is indistinguishable from a forgotten one, and this pair has now been out of
step for a month twice (#2606, #3180).
The reverse — a check the ruleset requires and Mergify does not wait for — is NOT declarable and
the guard refuses to accept a record for it. protect-dev has no bypass actors, so Mergify's
merge is refused by GitHub after the queue has already decided the PR is ready: a stuck entry
with nothing red to explain it. There is no state of the world in which that is what someone
meant, and an escape hatch for it would only make it a habit.
SHRINK-ONLY. A record that no longer corresponds to a real divergence is an integrity failure,
the same rule demos/proofs/ledger-baseline.json and infra/template-parity-exclusions.yaml carry:
a record for something that does not exist is the same stale-evidence shape it was meant to
expose. Deleting this file does not silence the guard — absent means empty, so every undeclared
lead becomes a failure.
EMPTY IS THE CORRECT STEADY STATE. It is empty today because the two lists agree exactly.
Add a record only while a check is deliberately ahead of the ruleset, and delete it in the PR
that lands the apply.
